_comment: Single source of truth for macro indicators (Plan A Tier 1). NOT YET wired into index.html render — see PLAN-macro-json.md for remaining steps. Each value carries a 'source' = the FRED / Trading Economics series ID it will auto-fetch from in Tier 2.

us10y.label: US 10Y Treasury
us10y.note: spiked to ~5.02% intraday 15 Sept (highest since 2007) on the confirmed Fed hike, then eased to ~4.93–4.94% by week's end as the initial shock faded

fedFunds.label: Fed Funds Rate
fedFunds.note: first hike in 3 years, unanimous FOMC decision; the Fed's own Summary of Economic Projections points to at least one more hike before year-end

usCPI.label: US CPI (YoY)
usCPI.note: carried forward from three weeks ago — flagged for next session's sweep

usPCE.label: US PCE (YoY)
usPCE.note: not independently re-verified this cycle; watch alongside the next CPI print

dxy.label: Dollar Index (DXY)
dxy.note: carried forward from three weeks ago; flagged for next session given the scale of the rate move since

source.caveat: DXY proper is ICE; DTWEXBGS is FRED's broad trade-weighted USD index — close proxy, label accordingly

biRate.label: Bank Indonesia Rate
biRate.note: carried forward; local desks now frame September as sideways-to-bearish for IHSG rather than a straight-line extension — flagged for next session's IHSG/BBCA-specific re-check

usdidr.label: USD/IDR
usdidr.note: assessed as stable, holding roughly Rp17,400–17,500 — a touch firmer than three weeks ago despite the confirmed Fed hike

gold.label: Gold (XAU)
gold.delta: slipped further, still no hedge bid
gold.note: eased to roughly $4,270-4,280 even as the 10Y hit an 18-year high and the oil crisis deepened — firm dollar + high real yields still outweighing haven demand; still well below January's ~$5,300–5,600 record

source.caveat: no free FRED/TE daily series; keep manual or use a market-data API in a later tier

wti.label: WTI Crude
wti.delta: multi-month high on a real supply shock
wti.note: the 11 Sept East-West Crude Oil Pipeline shutdown plus renewed Hormuz/Bab-al-Mandab disruption pushed WTI to roughly $99-100 — reportedly among the largest supply disruptions on record. A 16-17 Sept Iran-Oman Strait-reopening plan plus Trump's 'nearing the end' comments are a genuine but unconfirmed de-escalation thread — treat as elevated and two-sided, not resolved
